data.abstract: Identifying the origin of memory poisoning is essential for containment and system recovery. This study develops a temporal traceability model to detect and localize poisoning sources in distributed agent systems. A time-indexed memory influence matrix is constructed to quantify causal propagation strength between agents. Granger causality testing combined with sparse regression identifies probable poisoning origins. Experiments were performed on simulated collaborative planning systems with 80 agents and controlled adversarial injection points. Source attribution accuracy reached 91.2%, and containment strategies reduced secondary contamination by 54.6% within 15 update iterations. The proposed framework improves forensic analysis and containment efficiency in adversarial multi-agent environments.
